content.user_title: Improve UX With Research-Led Design Guidance
content.value_statement: Teams often design flows from assumptions and miss accessibility issues. This skill guides research, structure, interaction design, and review using UX best practices.
actual_capabilities: Plans user interviews with open-ended questions and synthesis steps.
Creates personas, journey maps, and user flows from provided research data.
Reviews screens and flows against WCAG AA accessibility expectations.
Organizes navigation, labels, and content using information architecture rules.
Drafts clearer microcopy, error states, empty states, and confirmation dialogs.
Applies visual hierarchy, spacing, typography, and design system guidance.
limitations: It cannot conduct real user interviews unless you provide participant data or transcripts.
It does not replace a formal legal or compliance accessibility audit.
It gives design guidance, not production-ready Figma files by itself.
Its recommendations depend on the product context and evidence you provide.

use_cases.title: Plan a Research Study
use_cases.description: Create interview goals, open-ended questions, recruiting criteria, and synthesis steps before design work starts.

use_cases.title: Review a Product Flow
use_cases.description: Evaluate onboarding, checkout, settings, or account flows for usability, recovery paths, and clear microcopy.

use_cases.title: Improve Accessibility
use_cases.description: Check a design against core WCAG AA expectations, touch targets, keyboard access, labels, and inclusive patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Start a UX Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing screen or flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this screen or flow for UX issues. Focus on user goals, clarity, accessibility, and the next best improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan User Interviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a user interview plan for this product idea. Include research goals, participant criteria, open-ended questions, and synthesis steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Better Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate flow redesign with edge cases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this user flow. Map the happy path, decision points, error states, recovery paths, and progress indicators.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Design System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across patterns and components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these design system components for accessibility, interaction states, responsive behavior, visual hierarchy, and documentation gaps.

output_examples.input: Review a four-step SaaS onboarding flow with email verification before workspace setup.
output: Issue: Email verification blocks users before they see value.
Recommendation: Let setup continue and show a reminder banner until verification is complete.
Accessibility check: Add visible labels, focus states, and screen reader status updates.

output_examples.input: Create interview questions for a mobile grocery reorder feature.
output: Research goal: Understand how shoppers repeat common purchases.
Question: Walk me through the last time you reordered groceries on your phone.
Synthesis: Cluster observations by trigger, friction point, and workaround.

output_examples.input: Improve empty state copy for a project dashboard with no projects.
output: Better copy: No projects yet. Create your first project to organize tasks and files.

best_practices: Start with user evidence before choosing layouts or components.
Check accessibility, error recovery, and responsive behavior for every important flow.
Provide enough product context, target users, constraints, and current designs for useful recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not create personas from demographics alone.
Do not use color as the only way to show status, errors, or selection.
Do not ask for a visual redesign without sharing user goals or task context.

faq.question: Can this skill create wireframes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline low, mid, and high-fidelity wireframe structures from your goals and constraints.

faq.question: Does it perform real user research?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan research and synthesize provided findings, but it cannot interview users by itself.

faq.question: Can it review accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks common WCAG AA concerns, labels, keyboard access, touch targets, contrast, and inclusive design patterns.

faq.question: Is it useful for developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can clarify component states, edge cases, interaction behavior, and handoff details for implementation.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the target user, task, current flow, screenshots or descriptions, constraints, and any research findings.

faq.question: Can it replace a UX designer?
faq.answer: No. It supports design thinking and review, but expert judgment and real user validation remain important.
